jobs.description:
Career Area

Technology, Digital and Data

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Who is CAT Digital? What do we do?

Big machines require big thinking. Are you looking for your next big challenge?

Cat® Digital is the digital and technology arm of Caterpillar Inc., leveraging the latest technologies, data and AI to build industry leading digital solutions for our customers and dealers. With over one million connected assets worldwide, our teams use data, technology, advanced analytics, telematics, and AI capabilities to help our customers build a better world.

Working with a Fortune 100 leader, you can build your career on a global scale and take advantage of development opportunities with emerging technologies. We’ve created an inclusive environment for you to explore your passions, make an impact and do the work that really matters. Join Us.

Job Opportunity

We are seeking talented individuals to join our team to help us grow our presence, organization, culture, which will drive our digital product development efforts. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies and collaborate with top professionals working on very high impact and visibility products. Don't miss this chance to join a forming presence and support digital innovation for a global leader in heavy machinery!

What will you do?

We are excied to offer one-year fixed-term position
at Cat Digital. As Data Scientist
, you will work on analytical tasks and projects on huge amounts of data to support data-driven business decisions and development. You will be a part of the team that utilizes AI, data science and statistical analysis to gain insight into asset condition monitoring as well as market and customer behaviors to support aftermarket businesses.

Your Responsibility Will Involve Understanding Existing Data Pipelines And Algorithms To Provide Technical And Business Support, With The Goal To Enhance And Optimize Them With New Techniques And Models. You Will As Well

Assist the implementation of next-generation techniques (such as weak learning, time series, NLP) supported by AI and agents, including tests, validation and delivery
Explore and implement innovative and advanced statistical approaches to improve and transform solutions, including Large Language Model (LLM) concepts and prompt engineering techniques to solve business challenges.
Provide support and explainability to technical partners as well as business partners to drive adoption
Create documentation, compelling presentations and visualizations to explain complex technical algorithms and impacts into understandable business language

What You Have

Bachelor/Master or PhD degree (statistics, mathematics, physics, economics, biology or a similar field)
Relevant professional experience utilizing quantitative analysis and AI is an advantage
Experience with modern GenAI frameworks including LangChain, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, and CrewAI is an advantage
Experience in using Data visualization tools to convey and simplify complex concepts into business value and actions
Solid background in using SQL and Python, knowledge of advanced statistical models and methods, fluency in AI as well as curiosity to explore and learn more.
Knowledge of ML operationalization (Airflow, Great Expectations, etc.) is an advantage
Ability to clearly communicate complex technical ideas, regardless of the technical capacity of the audience.

We are looking for someone who can work independently as well as part of a team, who can communicate effectively and efficiently with business partners, and is willing to take ownership of their work. If you have a passion for problem-solving and are constantly looking for ways to optimize processes, we encourage you to apply for this role.

What We Offer

From day one, you’re set up to thrive at Caterpillar: helpful training, relatable mentors, global experience, competitive salary package, work-life balance, and the growth opportunities you expect with a Fortune 100 company. You power our success, and we are committed to empowering yours. After all, when your work can impact the entire world, it’s important to do work that matters.

Additional Information

The position has fixed-term contract (12 months)
A valid Swiss work permit or Swiss or EU-25/EFTA citizenship is required for this position.
There is no relocation and no Visa sponsorship

We value authenticity and encourage candidates to submit original, personally crafted responses throughout our hiring process. Use of AI-generated content may disadvantage your application.

Please frequently check the email associated with your application, including the junk/spam folder, as this is the primary correspondence method. If you wish to know the status of your application – please use the candidate log-in on our career website as it will reflect any updates to your status.

Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for all positions without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, age, national origin, citizenship status, marital status, military/veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, physical or mental disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Caterpillar is committed to creating a dynamic work environment that values diversity and inclusion, respect and integrity, customer focus, and innovation. For more information, visit https://www.caterpillar.com/en/careers/why-caterpillar.html

Follow us on Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube.

This position requires working onsite five days a week.

jobs.description:
MSAT PPS Engineer – Precision Dispensing & Sensor Manufacturing (m/f/d)

Manufacturing Science & Technology (MSAT) serves as the global enabling function for the Sensors & Cartridges (S&C) network. Our mandate spans from supporting early-stage concept ideas to delivering seamless design transfers into routine manufacturing and driving sustainable product care across the entire product lifecycle.
We are organized into technology areas and multidisciplinary Squads supported by Chapters. By combining deep technical expertise, continuous learning, and systems thinking, we constantly improve manufacturing operations across our global network. Our daily collaboration is grounded in four core values: Courage, Transparency, Open-Mindedness, and a Can-Do Attitude.
Based at our site in Rotkreuz, this role sits within the Product & Process Science (PPS) group. You will apply hands-on precision dispensing expertise directly where it matters most: on the production floor, working shoulder-to-shoulder with process engineers, shift operators, and quality teams to stabilize processes, minimize scrap, and boost product quality.

The Perfect Candidate: has expertise in (electro-chemical) sensors, sensor manufacturing or (electro-, analytical-, technical) chemistry. He/She is knowledgeable about processes in the chemical labs, manufacturing and quality control. The candidate is familiar with leading continuous improvement projects and used data science (programming, statistics etc.) in previous roles or projects to support data-driven decisions. The role includes communication, collaboration and alignment with interfaces ranging from the engineering team to shopfloor, which the candidate brings with him.

General Information:

Start Date: to be discussed
Planned Duration of Employment: unlimited contract via Hays
Workplace: Rotkreuz
Workload: 100%
Home Office: most unlikely
Travel: no

Tasks & Responsibilities

Conduct on-the-ground investigations across the manufacturing line to identify root causes of WIP yield loss, downtime, and dispensing-related deviations; design and execute concrete remediation plans.
Spend consistent, hands-on time on the production floor observing multi-shift runs, partnering closely with operators and shift leads, and upskilling staff from an engineering perspective.
Fine-tune, characterize, and troubleshoot multi-platform automated dispensing equipment, with an emphasis on low-viscosity fluid behavior, surface interaction, and tight tolerances.
Plan, run, and evaluate production-line trials, applying structured problem-solving (e.g., DOE, root-cause methodology) to stabilize fluid deposition and process repeatability.
Analyze sensor production and quality control data to track variability, spot drifting parameters early, and prove the statistical effectiveness of corrective actions.
Act as the technical translator between equipment vendors, shop-floor operators, Process Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Regulatory Compliance to implement sustainable change controls.

Must Haves:

Deep Precision Dispensing Expertise (Min. 5+ Years). Practical, engineering-level experience in automated precision dispensing or fluid deposition, ideally with strong hands-on capability handling low-viscosity fluids. You have directly set up, fine-tuned, characterized, and troubleshot dispensing platforms (e.g., as a process development engineer, field application specialist, or vendor-facing integration expert)
A track record of turning troubleshooting into verifiable production improvements (e.g., scrap reduction, cycle-time stabilization, yield improvements) backed by data
You thrive at the machine side, enjoy working directly with operators across shifts, and communicate comfortably in an active manufacturing environment
A completed technical degree (BSc/MSc in Process, Mechanical, Chemical, Materials, or Biomedical Engineering) or a completed vocational/technical qualification backed by robust, relevant engineering-level experience. Proven technical competence and practical problem-solving capability take precedence over formal titles
Confident using root-cause analysis, basic statistical methods, and structured experimentation to make evidence-based decisions.
Solid understanding of material properties, dispensing parameters and equipment condition
Languages: Fluent English (working project language) combined with German skills at a minimum B2 level to communicate smoothly with shop-floor teams.

Nice to Haves

Experience within Life Sciences, Medical Devices, Diagnostics, or another highly regulated GxP/GMP manufacturing setting.
Familiarity with sensor manufacturing (e.g., electrochemical/analytical sensors, microassembly, functional coating, or cartridge assembly).
Experience conducting non-conformity/deviation investigations, CAPAs, and technical change-control documentation.
Hands-on familiarity with data tools for statistical process monitoring and data-driven troubleshooting.
Prior background working for or closely interfacing with precision dispensing equipment vendors or automated system integrators.

At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Data Scientist

London
4 days/week office
Up to £80,000 + bonus

The opportunity

Our client is a fast-growing intelligence business that helps senior Operations and Supply Chain leaders cut through the noise and make better decisions. They combine proprietary data, member research and AI-native analysis to answer the questions that keep C-suite executives up at night.

Right now they’re riding two of the biggest tailwinds in the market — AI and supply chain — which is a big part of why they’ve grown so quickly since raising funding last year. They’re still only around 100 people and firmly in scale-up mode, so roles here are broad rather than tightly boxed in, with real scope to shape what the position becomes. They want people who bring their own ideas about how things should work, not just execute a brief.

Alongside their Data & Insights function, they’re hiring a Data Scientist to help uncover what’s actually moving the needle on AI and digital adoption in supply chains, and turn that into intelligence their members can act on.

What you’ll actually do

A representative project: proving that specific AI, robotics, or technology implementations are actually having a positive commercial impact — for example, sourcing data points from 10-K filings on whether and how a company mentions a given AI, robotics, or technology implementation, combining that with financial performance data, and then running proper correlation and statistical work to find the patterns that are genuinely commercially relevant, not structuring data for its own sake, but using it to answer a real question about what’s driving outcomes.

It’s a fast-paced environment: you’ll typically have several different projects on the go each month rather than sinking weeks into a single piece of work, so it suits someone who likes variety and moving at pace. You’ll work closely with the Analyst and Research side of the team — they’ll sometimes bring you in on the final client-facing narrative, but the analytical thinking behind it, what the data is and isn’t telling you and why it matters, is yours.
What makes someone good at this

This isn’t a software engineering role — there’s a separate (currently paused) AI Engineer seat for that. It’s a data science and insight role: genuinely comfortable with ambiguity and messy data, and more interested in the “why” behind a correlation than in producing one and moving on.

The people who do well here use AI thoughtfully throughout their process — not just to speed up code, but to explore data, test approaches and sanity-check their own conclusions — while knowing exactly where to stop trusting the output and check it themselves.

Most come from a data science background with a genuinely commercial mindset: someone who has always cared more about the decision an analysis supports than the elegance of the model behind it. Self-starters do particularly well here — if you’ve ever looked at a question and gone and built the dataset yourself rather than waiting for a clean one to land in your lap, this role will make sense to you.

What you’ll need

Around 6-8 years in data science, applied statistics, or a closely related quantitative field — or a shorter track record if you’ve spent time building or running something of your own and are looking to bring that energy into a team
Strong Python and SQL, with real experience building and maintaining data pipelines and transformations, not just running ad hoc queries
Hands-on experience extracting structured data from messy or unstructured sources — documents, filings, scraped or third-party data — and getting it into an analysable state
Genuine statistical and quantitative method: correlation and relationship analysis, feature engineering, transformation logic — data science, not BI reporting
Comfortable in modern data environments (Databricks or equivalent)
Hands-on, critical fluency with AI-assisted development and analysis tools — using them to write code, explore data, and sanity-check findings, while always applying your own judgement on what to trust
Comfort with ambiguity: able to take a loosely scoped question, form your own hypothesis about what’s going on, and iterate toward a defensible answer without needing perfectly defined requirements from the outset
Supply chain or operations domain exposure is a genuine plus, not required

The package

Up to £80,000 plus a bonus scheme, private healthcare and life insurance, enhanced pension, enhanced parental leave and unlimited holiday. Based from a well appointed central London office four days a week, in a small, high trust team that moves fast, expects a lot, and gives a lot of room to grow into shaping what gets investigated next rather than just answering the brief as given.

Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model.

Why Now

Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services.

Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact.

You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now.

Machine Learning Engineer, Applied AI

About The Role

So much of the work society depends on is still slower and harder than it should be. Permits take months. Claims sit unresolved. And AI hasn't changed that — because the bottleneck isn't the models. It's the institutional context AI needs to do the work: rules, history, relationships, and judgment scattered across people, documents, and legacy systems.

BrainCo exists to fix that. We build agent-native operating systems for the institutions society depends on, and our products are the first of their kind in the world — we were the first, anywhere, to fully automate construction permitting, and we're now doing the same across insurance and other industries. There is no playbook here, because no one has built this before.

As a Machine Learning Engineer on Applied AI, your work begins where the demo ends: getting a model to look impressive is the easy part; making it a production decision system an institution stakes its process on is the job. The problems come in every shape — custom vision model pipelines that check blueprints against building codes at 95%+ accuracy, agents that untangle policy stacks to reveal coverage gaps, systems that predict from clinical records whether a patient is on their care path — and you'll own them end-to-end, from ambiguous customer problem to the eval that catches a whole class of errors.

This is frontier ML applied where it's hardest and matters most. The problems are underspecified, the documents are brutal, the accuracy bar is institutional-grade — and the feedback loops are real, because our systems move real workflows forward every day.

Who We're Looking For

You understand how machine learning actually works — not just the tooling, but the philosophy underneath: what a loss function really optimizes, how generalization breaks under distribution shift, why evaluation is where systems quietly go wrong. And you live at the bleeding edge of modern AI, with hard-won instincts for squeezing the most out of LLMs and agentic systems — prompting, fine-tuning, tool use, and reasoning. That combination is the job: you know when a fine-tuned segmentation model beats a VLM, when a rule engine beats both, and how to compose all three into a system more accurate than any single model. You treat frontier models as components to be measured, pushed, and engineered — never as magic.

Most of all, you're energized by building things that have never existed, and comfortable when the problem, the data, and the definition of success all have to be invented at once.

The Problems You'll Work On

Composite AI systems and credit assignment.
Our most demanding systems chain vision transformers, segmentation models, VLM reasoning, and rule engines. When the pipeline is wrong, which component failed? One of the most interesting open problems in applied ML.

Document understanding beyond the frontier.
Blueprints, site plans, policy stacks, contracts, clinical records — dense, multimodal documents that break off-the-shelf models. You'll build models that actually read them.

Agents that learn from real work.
Our deployments generate verified, ground-truth outcomes on every decision — reward signals most labs can only simulate. You'll help design the data, evals, and training loops to build and fine-tune agents on them.

Evaluation as a product discipline.
When a regulator has to trust your system, evals are the product. You'll build eval suites and failure-mode taxonomies rigorous enough to earn institutional sign-off.

Institutional Intelligence that compounds.
Every verified correction improves the system twice: the corrected fact percolates to every application, and the system that builds the intelligence learns to build it better. You'll work on both loops.

In This Role, You Will

Turn ambiguity into shipped systems
— from no problem statement, no labeled data, and no agreed definition of success, to well-posed ML problems and production deployments.

Own AI systems end-to-end.
There is no handoff: the person who trains the model owns its behavior in production.

Work at the research frontier with production stakes
, applying LLMs, RL fine-tuning, and agentic systems where the output is a decision an institution acts on.

Work directly with the institutions we serve
— permit reviewers, underwriters, compliance officers — to understand how decisions actually get made and ensure your systems change how the work gets done.

Engineer for production reality
, navigating accuracy, latency, cost, and reliability in environments far messier than any benchmark.

Raise the bar across the company
through design reviews, our internal paper club, and the shared playbook for AI systems institutions can trust.

Compensation

We pay competitively for every role and back that with meaningful equity, because we want the people building Brain Co. to genuinely share in what we build together. Beyond salary and equity, we invest in country-specific benefits because we want our team to feel taken care of, not only compensated.

The annual base salary range for this role is $190,000 - $325,000
. We publish this range for every role, as a matter of policy regardless of whether local law requires it. Actual pay will depend on skills, scope, and experience.

What We Offer

Joining Joybuy means becoming part of a business where people, innovation, and impact work together to shape the future of cross-border e-commerce. You’ll contribute to smart supply chains, efficient logistics, and meaningful projects that drive real customer value. With a competitive salary, great office locations, and a supportive, people-first culture, you’ll have the space to grow your career, learn from talented colleagues, and make a genuine impact in a fast-expanding international business.

You’ll be joining the Joybuy team, which values collaboration, ownership, and a commitment to delivering high-quality results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

We are seeking a data-driven and analytical Payment Operations & Risk Analyst to monitor, optimize, and protect our global payment ecosystem. In this role, you will be the frontline investigator tracking payment performance, mitigating fraud, and identifying areas to improve cost efficiency. You will collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Risk teams, translating complex transaction data into actionable improvements that safeguard company funds and enhance customer experience. If you love solving data puzzles, mapping out technical user journeys, and supporting international scaling, this role is for you.

What You Will Do

Order & Payment Scheme Design and Implementation Focus on the full-chain of cross-border e-commerce order transactions; lead the business solution design for platform transaction payments, order settlement, and receivables/collection disbursement. Deeply adapt to cross-border platform trading rules; deliver standardized transaction payment & settlement solutions tailored to different merchants, transaction scenarios and order types, supporting the scaled and standardized expansion of platform order transaction business.
Transaction Payment System Requirements & Development Deeply participate in iterative development and functional optimization of the order transaction payment system; focus on core transaction payment scenarios. Payment Service & Process Optimization Continuously review and address pain points across the end-to-end order transaction payment chain. Run dedicated optimization initiatives targeting key issues, including transaction payment failures, abnormal order settlement, delayed collection, stuck funds, transaction rejections, and compensation/dispute handling. Iterate on the transaction payment operational processes to drive up the overall order transaction success rate.
Cross-departmental Project Execution Coordinate with business, operations, risk control and technical teams to drive dedicated optimization projects for order transaction payment and settlement. Follow the full lifecycle of requirements review, system development, feature testing, pilot (gray) launch, acceptance and iteration to ensure the payment system capability matches the platform's order transaction business growth rhythm.
Transaction Data Review & Best-practice Accumulation Own monitoring and control of core payment data metrics, including transaction success rate, settlement timeliness, and abnormal transactions ratio. Complete issue attribution and performance review; issue regular transaction payment analysis reports. Accumulate standardized cross-border order transaction payment solutions, risk handling case studies chers, and best practices.

About You

Experience: 2-5 years of experience in payment operations, data analytics, fraud risk management, or a closely related role within fintech or e-commerce.
Payment Knowledge: Solid understanding of the fundamental payment lifecycle, including gateways, acquiring, card schemes, chargebacks, and settlements.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: London

About The Team

The Cloudflare Data Intelligence & Analytics (DIA) team has built a unified data & ML platform to provide our internal Business Partners with actionable analytics, insights, and recommendations.

Our goals are to:

Democratize data & intelligence for humans and agents
Build a context layer and an AI systems layer upon our unified data & content platform
Support Cloudflare’s critical business needs

Role Summary

We are looking for an experienced Data Analyst in London to scale our growth & adoption analytics initiatives. You will be a trusted data advisor to our business partners, a technical coach to your peers, and the lead in terms of shaping AI-first data models, workflows, and agent-ready-datasets.

Success in this role will rely on marrying a strong analytics background with product and business acumen to deliver highly strategic and compelling insights that accelerate growth and influence adoption. This role also requires a deep understanding of data infrastructure, job orchestration, and lineage, all with the use of AI-tooling as default.

Own the development and maintenance of agent-ready curated datasets end-to-end

To support the rollout and ongoing maintenance of the EMEA RCSA framework and related internal control activities, we are looking for an RCSA & Internal Control Analyst to join the team. Working alongside the EMEA Risk & Control Manager, the successful candidate will provide day-to-day operational support, including coordination, follow-up, documentation and data consolidation. This will help accelerate the rollout, improve consistency across countries and establish a sustainable long-term operating model, while allowing the EMEA Risk & Control Manager to remain focused on governance, stakeholder management and overall framework oversight.

The role will support the rollout, documentation, testing and maintenance of country-level Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) and related internal control activities across EMEA. Support the implementation and ongoing development of the EMEA Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) framework, working with country teams to identify, assess and manage risks in line with the Group's risk management methodology.

Support the identification and assessment of country-specific risks, documenting existing controls, potential gaps and compensating controls to help ensure risks are appropriately managed.
Develop and maintain local risk and control registers, ensuring information is accurate, up to date and aligned with regional requirements.
Work with local stakeholders to harmonise risk management approaches and control frameworks across EMEA, promoting consistency while taking account of country-specific requirements and differences in local maturity.
Support the implementation of the RCSA framework across EMEA countries, coordinating activities, gathering and consolidating information, monitoring progress and following up with stakeholders to ensure timely completion.
Support second-line (Line 2) control testing activities, including coordinating evidence collection, reviewing supporting documentation and following up on outstanding information or identified control gaps.
Contribute to compliance activities, including the ongoing monitoring and documentation of anti-corruption and accounting controls in support of Sapin II requirements.
Track action plans, remediation activities and outstanding issues, working with local stakeholders to monitor progress, address delays and ensure agreed actions are completed.
Build effective working relationships across countries and functions, encouraging collaboration, knowledge-sharing and consistent approaches to risk management in an international, matrixed organisation.
Identify opportunities to improve risk and control processes, documentation and procedures, contributing to the continuous development of a consistent and sustainable EMEA control framework.

Educational Qualifications

A degree or equivalent professional experience in Risk Management, Business, Finance, Compliance or a related discipline would be advantageous.
Ongoing commitment to training and professional development in risk, compliance and audit processes.

Relevant Skills And Experience

2–5 years' experience in risk management, internal controls, compliance or a related field.
Experience working with risk and compliance frameworks, including risk identification, assessment and control implementation.
Experience working in an international business or matrix organisation, engaging stakeholders across multiple countries and functions.
Good understanding of operational processes and internal controls across different business functions.
Strong organisational, analytical and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and build effective working relationships.
Confident managing documentation, risk registers, trackers and supporting evidence, with strong attention to detail.
Able to work autonomously, take ownership of tasks and manage competing deadlines.

Resilient and adaptable: Comfortable navigating challenges, working through ambiguity and maintaining momentum when faced with competing priorities or differing levels of risk maturity across countries.
Curious and analytical: Naturally inquisitive, with the confidence to ask questions, challenge assumptions and develop an understanding of risks across different business functions.

Structured in approach: Able to bring order to complex or ambiguous situations, organise information clearly and establish consistent ways of working.

Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on.

Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Adanola and Huel use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform — and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.

About The Role

We're looking for a Data Scientist
to join Fospha's Data Science team in London.

Fospha builds marketing measurement products for ecommerce brands — attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact measurement. Our Data Science team owns the models behind all of it, from methodology through to production code. You will work across our technical stacks and own maintaining and growing the codebases that power our product and solutions.

This role suits an established data scientist who wants to own things properly. You'll lead larger production projects, choose the modelling approach rather than being handed it, and talk to clients as the modelling expert in the room — supported by a team that reviews each other's work seriously, and a company that rewards high agency with ownership.

Team:
Data Science

Level:
Career (Data Science Career Development Framework)

Location:
London

What you'll do

Lead larger production projects end to end — scoping, building, and shipping production-level code, rather than working through tickets someone else has specified
Choose the modelling approach — independently selecting and applying the right method within our suite, across attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact. You will be given time to keep up-to-date on the latest methodologies in the industry
Resolve bugs and queries independently — including in parts of the codebase you didn't write, without needing to route them upwards
Use AI as leverage, not as a crutch — solving coding tickets quickly, unblocking yourself on product and engineering dependencies, and building automation workflows that save the team time
Work with QA properly — using our automated tooling efficiently and flagging the gaps in it rather than working around them
Communicate as a modelling expert — confidently and independently, with clients and with colleagues, including when the message is that a number they like is wrong
Help develop the people around you — code review, methodology critique, and hands-on support for less experienced colleagues. Breaking down tickets and helping those more junior is essential

What we're looking for

Essential

Solid commercial data science experience — typically 3–5 years, with a track record of shipping models into production
Strong ML knowledge across multiple algorithm families, and the judgement to pick the right approach for the problem rather than the one you know best
Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to lead on production-level code and set the standard others work to
Able to debug and resolve issues independently across unfamiliar repositories, using AI tooling to accelerate rather than to guess, while still understanding the problem fully
Strong AI fluency — you solve tickets quickly with it, you unblock cross-department dependencies with it, you build automation workflows with it, and you never send AI-assisted output without checking it
Confident, independent communication with clients and stakeholders as the technical authority on the work
Emerging mentorship — you're ready to develop junior colleagues, and you want to
Initiative in accepting and planning your own work, rather than waiting to be allocated it
Genuine attention to detail — much of this work involves noticing when a number is wrong

Nice to have

Bayesian modelling experience, particularly hierarchical models
Experience with AWS or comparable cloud tooling
Familiarity with automated QA tooling and test coverage practices
Experience with marketing, ecommerce, or advertising data

Not required

Experience with attribution methodology, MMM, incrementality testing, or Bayesian modelling is genuinely an advantage at this level — but it isn't a filter. Our stack takes time to learn regardless of what you arrive with, and we'd rather hire strong modelling judgement and teach the domain.

How You'll Grow

We run a published Data Science Career Development Framework with six levels. You'd join at Career, where the expectations are:

AI Fluency & Tooling:
Leverages AI to solve coding tickets quickly; consistently unblocks themselves on cross-department dependencies, especially product and engineering; never sends AI-assisted communication without checking quality; expert at using AI to build automation workflows.

Machine Learning & Modelling:
Strong ML knowledge across multiple algorithm families; independently chooses and applies the right modelling approach within Fospha's suite.

Engineering & Codebase:
Leads on larger coding projects and tickets with production-level code; resolves queries and bugs efficiently and independently; master at using supplied AWS tooling through AI; uses automated QA tools efficiently and flags gaps to the QA team.

Stakeholder & Communication:
Confidently and independently communicates with clients and colleagues as a modelling expert; assists with the development of junior members of staff.

Job Complexity:
Consistent contributor and respected knowledge holder, with emerging collaboration and mentorship abilities.

Supervision:
Demonstrates initiative in accepting and planning work.

Progression to Advanced
level is against explicit, published criteria — taking on almost any ticket efficiently, building and planning production repositories, collaborating with product on project outcomes and estimates, actively developing junior colleagues, and representing Fospha as a trusted external voice on modelling in senior client and partner conversations. You'll know what you're working towards from your first week.

Throughout, we look for the same core behaviours: concise communication, collaboration, problem solving, critical thinking, growth mindset, attention to detail, time management, and initiative.

Why Fospha

Real methodological depth. Bayesian attribution, MMM, geo lift testing, and causal inference are our day job, not a side project. You'll be working on all of it, not adjacent to it.
Ownership at the methodology level. At this level you're choosing the approach, not implementing someone else's choice.
Published career framework. No guessing what the next level requires or when you'll get there.
A team that reviews each other's work properly. Code review and methodology critique from people who care about getting the model right.
Direct client impact. The models you build and maintain drive real budget decisions at brands you'll recognise.

jobs.title: Research Associate in Biomedical Engineering
jobs.description:
The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

Overview

Are you a passionate researcher eager to bridge the gap between advanced engineering and clinical practice to tackle a transformative healthcare challenge? We have an exciting opportunity in the School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering for a Research Associate to apply their skills in biomedical engineering to revolutionize haemodialysis and make a profound impact on global health.

You will join the Thermofluids Group at the University of Sheffield, working in close collaboration with experts in the School of Medicine and Population Health and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. As a key member of this interdisciplinary project, you will lead the design, assembly, and clinical validation of a novel dialyser prototype.

You will be responsible for testing the prototype using blood-mimicking fluids and, ultimately, human blood to assess cleaning efficiency, clotting risk, and biocompatibility.

This role offers a unique opportunity to apply fundamental engineering principles to real-world physiological conditions. You will work in close collaboration with two other Research Associates focusing on numerical simulations and experimental fluid dynamics, contributing directly to a greener, more efficient future for nephrology.

Main Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the assembly of the prototype, ensuring tight tolerances for spinning components, robust sealing, and integration of semi-permeable membranes. You will troubleshoot technical issues during assembly to ensure the prototype is ready for testing.
Conduct rigorous solute removal efficiency tests using Human Peripheral Simulated Blood Plasma (BZ464). You will measure the clearance rates of key metabolites, including urea, creatinine, and phosphate, to optimize the operational parameters of the dialyser.
Manage the ethical procurement and testing of voluntarily donated human blood to assess biocompatibility. You will evaluate the prototype for fibrin strands, check transmembrane pressure, and analyse blood samples for clotting and haemolysis markers, ensuring safety standards are met.
Work closely with the fluids engineering PDRAs to translate simulation and experimental results into physiological insights. You will actively participate in weekly meetings with renal clinicians at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals to interpret data and refine the device design based on clinical feedback.
Maintain meticulous records of experimental methodologies and results in compliance with clinical governance frameworks. You will contribute to the writing of high-impact journal publications, present outcomes at international medical and engineering conferences, and participate in public engagement events regarding sustainable nephrology.

jobs.description:
The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

The School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences is seeking to appoint a Research Associate in Theoretical Cosmology. This post is funded by the Royal Society through Dr Eleonora Di Valentino’s Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship renewal for the project “H0 Tension Test” (H0TTEST) and is fixed term for 12 months.

The project investigates whether tensions in cosmological observations, particularly the Hubble constant tension, arise from unaccounted-for systematic effects or indicate new physics beyond the standard ΛCDM model. It combines theoretical modelling, cosmological data analysis and numerical methods to explore extensions involving dark energy, dark matter, neutrino physics, inflation and modified gravity. You will contribute to testing cosmological models with current observations and assessing their predictions for forthcoming surveys, with scope to develop research directions that reflect your expertise and interests within the project’s aims.

You will work with Dr Eleonora Di Valentino within the Cosmology, Relativity and Gravitation group, which comprises five academic staff (Dr Eleonora Di Valentino, Dr Sam Dolan, Dr Steffen Gielen, Professor Carsten van de Bruck and Professor Elizabeth Winstanley) and six PhD students. The group’s expertise spans cosmology, gravitation and mathematical physics, with an active seminar programme and close links to colleagues in statistics and astrophysics, providing a stimulating environment to develop your research career. Funds will be available to support professional development, including participation in conferences, collaboration meetings and research visits.

You should have a PhD in physics, astronomy, cosmology or a closely related discipline, or equivalent experience. We welcome candidates with a strong research background in cosmology and expertise in one or more of the following: cosmological data analysis, statistical inference, theoretical modelling or numerical simulations. We are looking for evidence of research achievement and potential, strong computational and analytical skills, and the ability to develop independent ideas and work collaboratively.

Main Duties And Responsibilities

Contribute to and support the work of the research group (e.g. by giving and attending local working seminars and participating in collaborations).

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a newly formed Private Cloud team. We are responsible for the design, deployment and operations of a new greenfield on-prem private cloud based on OpenStack.
The Private Cloud HPC Network Engineer will help design, build and evolve the high-performance network architecture underpinning our Private Cloud platform that will be used for HPC workloads.
The role combines deep data-centre and HPC networking expertise with modern cloud networking, software-defined infrastructure and automation. As part of the Private Cloud team, you will collaborate closely with compute, storage, platform engineering teams to deliver a scalable, resilient and highly automated cloud infrastructure.

Responsibilities:
* Design and evolve network architecture, standards and patterns for large-scale Private Cloud Openstack and HPC environments. Develop scalable Leaf-Spine architectures using technologies including BGP, EVPN, VXLAN and ECMP.

London, UK (primarily remote, with office visits 1–2 times a month)

Carbon markets only work if people can trust the data behind them. At CarbonAI we bring together project data, pricing, ratings and thousands of registry and methodology documents so buyers, investors and developers can make better decisions about carbon credits.

We're looking for a Data Engineer to own the pipelines that power this. You'll pull data from APIs, files and the web, turn complex documents into material our AI can use, and decide how it all gets built. We hire smart, careful people who communicate well, and then we give them real ownership.

Build and run Python pipelines that collect data from APIs, CSVs and other structured sources

Learn quickly and enjoy figuring out unfamiliar data and tricky problems
Take care over the details, finish what you start, and leave things well documented

Like owning a problem from start to finish, without waiting to be told each step

3-5 years' experience in data engineering or a similar role
Strong, production-quality Python

Experience pulling data from REST APIs and files such as CSV, Excel and JSON
Web scraping experience (e.g. BeautifulSoup, Scrapy or Playwright)
Experience extracting content from PDFs and other documents
Hands-on experience chunking documents for RAG

AWS or Azure
Infrastructure-as-Code
Embeddings and vector databases (RAG)
Measuring and improving retrieval quality
An interest in climate or carbon markets (no prior knowledge needed)

What we offer

Real ownership of the systems you build, and a say in tools and architecture
A small team that trusts people, with clear goals and no micromanagement
Work that makes carbon markets more transparent and more trustworthy
Room to grow into AI engineering or wider platform work
Primarily remote working, with occasional visits to our London office

jobs.description:
Über uns

Bei VREY
bauen wir das EnergyOS für Mehrfamilienhäuser
.
In Deutschland stehen über 3,3 Millionen Mehrparteienhäuser
– und sie sind das schwarze Loch der Energiewende. <1% Solardurchdringung. <2% Smart Metering. Kaum Flexibilität oder intelligentes Energiemanagement.
Gleichzeitig zwingt die Regulierung Eigentümer zu massiven Investitionen: Solar wird zur Pflicht, Smart Meter müssen in den nächsten 5 Jahren flächendeckend ausgerollt werden, Heizung und Mobilität elektrifizieren sich. Das Mehrfamilienhaus wird vom Betongold zum aktiven Teil der dezentralen Energieinfrastruktur.
Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.
VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software
und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).
Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:
Zweistellige Renditen und Wertsteigerung für Eigentümer,

~20 % Stromkostenersparnis für Mieter,
und
digitale Infrastruktur für Speicher, Wärmepumpen und Flexibilität.

Bereits heute betreuen wir eine dreistellige Anzahl an Projekten - darunter die größten Bestandshalter und Wohnungsbaugenossenschaften - in allen 16 Bundesländern. Damit gehören wir nach kürzester Zeit zu den führenden Anbietern im Markt.
Im Zuge unserer Seed-Finanzierung haben wir 3,3 Mio. € von führenden Impact- und Energy-VCs
(u. a. Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, Kopa Ventures) eingesammelt. Mit dem frischen Kapital gehen wir in die nächste Wachstumsphase und bauen unser Team gezielt aus.
Wir stehen am Anfang eines strukturellen Marktumbruchs. Wer heute die Energieinfrastruktur im Mehrfamilienhaus definiert, prägt sie für Jahrzehnte. Werde Teil von VREY und baue mit uns das führende EnergyOS.

Dein Profil

Du hast bereits erste Erfahrungen im Consulting (Tier 1/Tier 2)
, High-Growth Start-ups (
idealerweise Operations oder Prozessoptimierung),

Du strebst danach, die beste Version deiner selbst zu werden und suchst Umgebungen, in denen du dein volles Potenzial entfalten kannst

Du sprichst Deutsch und Englisch fließend

Mission der Rolle
Du unterstützt unser Team bei der operativen Umsetzung und Weiterentwicklung unserer Kundenprojekte.
Dein Ziel: Unsere Projektleiter:innen bei der Umsetzung unterstützen, interne Prozesse weiterentwickeln und datenbasierte Entscheidungen ermöglichen. Dabei wirst du ein tiefes Verständnis für Energieprojekte, Operations und Business-Aufbau entwickeln.

As Product Owner Service Resolution & Automation, you change that. Where cases still need people, you make the handover between call center, station, and other teams seamless. You work within our Customer Service Transformation, alongside Software Engineering, Data Science, and operations stakeholders, on top of an ecosystem that includes Salesforce, Genesys, and Conversational AI.

If you enjoy turning complex, manual operational processes into automated products and owning outcomes in a fast-paced environment, this role is for you!

Complaint capture & processing

Workflow automation
You design and deliver automated workflows with AI agents that independently validate each complaint, decide the outcome based on a decision matrix, and trigger the resolution. Full automation is the goal, manual handling the exception
System integration
You integrate with our rental software and branch workflow systems so processes are handed over seamlessly between customer service and frontline operations, with no manual rework or lost context
Product vision & roadmap

jobs.title: Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Why this role matters

Europe needs flexible capacity, and it needs it fast. Every new wind farm and solar park needs storage to keep the grid stable – and that is exactly what we build. Delta Capacity invests in, develops and operates large-scale standalone battery storage (BESS) across Germany, Finland, Sweden, Italy and Spain. We enter projects in early stages – greenfield, ready-to-build (RTB), EPC-ready – and take them through procurement, financing and construction to operation.  From RTB, our projects reach COD in ca. 15 months: our two Finnish projects, 125 MW / 300 MWh each, are heading for COD in Q4 2027.

We are looking for a Financial Analyst who loves building models that decisions rest on. Working hand in hand with our Investment Manager, you turn project data into valuations, investment cases and financing structures – and get a front-row seat to how large-scale battery storage is bought, financed and built.

What you will achieve in your first 12 months

Know our financial models inside out and keep them up to date, so any question from management, investors or lenders gets a fast, reliable answer.
Deliver the first valuation of new projects – revenue, capex, opex and returns.
Support at least one acquisition and one financing from kick-off to closing, from data room to final model.
Prepare investment committee papers and lender presentations that are clear, consistent and ready to go.

What you will do

Financial modelling and valuation

Build and maintain project and portfolio models for BESS – revenue stacking across tolling, ancillary services and trading, capex, opex, tax and debt.
Run scenarios and sensitivities on price curves, degradation, availability and financing terms, and show what really drives the returns.
Size debt and test it against lender metrics such as DSCRs and LLCRs, and keep the models audit-ready for model auditors and lenders.
Support portfolio valuation and reporting to our investors and shareholders.

Transaction support

Support due diligence end to end – data room, Q&A, red-flag tracking and input from legal, technical and tax advisors.
Prepare investment committee memos, term sheets, NBOs and lender presentations.
Benchmark offers, Supply agreements, EPC and LTSA prices and market data to sharpen our negotiation position.
Keep deal trackers and closing checklists up to date, so nothing falls through the cracks.

What you bring

3+ years in transaction services, corporate finance, project finance, investment banking or an infrastructure or private equity fund.
Excellent Excel and financial modelling skills; you know DCF, IRR, debt sculpting, sensitivities, refinancing. Python or VBA is a plus.
A degree in finance, economics, business or engineering, and a genuine interest in energy scale-up and battery storage. CFA or equivalent qualification is a plus.
Precision, ownership and the drive to learn fast in a small team.
Fluent English and German (C1)

What we offer

A steep learning curve – real deals, real models and real responsibility from your first week, with close coaching by an Investment Manager.
Direct impact on Europe's energy transition – your models turn into batteries that keep the grid stable and green.
A competitive remuneration and a path to grow into an investment role.
Hybrid working from our Munich office, with occasional travel across our European markets.
A small, high-trust team that moves fast, celebrates wins together and still makes time for ski trips and Oktoberfest.

jobs.description:
Only about 1% of our applicants end up in the offer stage. To increase your chances, give yourself a competitive edge and come fully prepared!

In a nutshell

As we are building the best milkman on earth, we are looking for sharp minds that can help us further shape Picnic as we expand across Europe. We are looking for experienced hires with a background in top strategy consulting, private equity, investment banking, e-commerce or commercial roles, that can tackle challenges and growth opportunities at Picnic.

Tricks of the trade

Lead with ambition: Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.
Steep learning curve: Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.
Solve real-life puzzles: Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.
Innovate across borders: You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.
High-performance environment: You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.

Your superpowers

Master’s degree in Econometrics, Engineering, Finance, Math or an equivalent quantitative study
2-5 years of work experience in top tier management consulting, PE, investment banking, retail topics and hands-on deal experience
Out-of-the-box thinking and initiative: hands-on, nothing-is-impossible mindset
Strong communication skills in German and English, allowing you to explain complex analytical concepts in a simple and practical way
Proficient with SQL and Python or excited to learn

Picnic Perks

🏆 Rewarding Impact from Day One

You’ll receive an attractive compensation package, designed to reward your ambition, drive, and the direct impact you’ll make from your very first project.

🍎Learning & development

You'll always have something to learn with us! You’ll benefit from opportunities like Lepaya training for polishing soft skills or Picnic Tech Academy training in case you want to learn new skills other than what you already know. We also offer free access to trained psychologists via our OpenUp partner, and German language classes if you’d like to get your experience in Germany to the next level.

🗺️Relocation

If you’re moving from another country to join Picnic we make it as smooth as possible for you. We’ll cover your flight costs and a first month's accommodation.

🥗Fresh Lunch, coffee, and snacks

Our offices are equipped with fully-fledged coffee bars and a kitchen. We get delicious fresh and warm lunches every day so you can keep your energy up.

⛳All the rest

At Picnic you get 30 holidays, we cover your travel expenses and offer a pension plan. And your phone and laptop are on us, of course.

FAQ

Which team will I join?

At Picnic, we build almost everything in-house. This means that we have plenty of opportunities for you in terms of project topics. Your interest lies in consumer topics like pricing, assortment, customer life time value? Or rather in logistics, supply chain, automated warehousing areas? Or you'd love going adventurous into new areas as long as you're solving real world problems? Let's talk and figure it out where there's the best match.

What are the long term opportunities for this role? What happens after I'm done with a project?

You get full accountability from the start: from shaping the strategy and driving step-change improvements, to collaborating with multiple teams to achieve tangible business results.

At Picnic, the long-term opportunity isn't just a role—it’s a platform to shape your own career trajectory with real ownership, business impact, and fast growth. Hence the career paths are as diverse as your ambitions. Depending on your interests and strengths, these are most common career paths we’ve seen so far:

Given our scale-up environment, many projects tend to grow in scope and complexity under your responsibility and you naturally grow a team around you in order to take your project to a next level.
As you grow, you’ll deepen your understanding of the business, build a strong internal network, and prove your ability to lead impactful projects. Once you feel you’ve learned everything in your scope and your projects have been successfully implemented, you can switch to complete different areas of Picnic. We have numerous colleagues that have switched from Commercial to Fulfillment, or from Distribution to Customer and many other examples.

Please send your application in English.

jobs.title: De Rijksoverheid zoekt: Data Engineer Workforce Management
jobs.description:
Op deze pagina:

Dit ga je doen
Dit krijg je
Dit bieden we nog meer
Dit vragen wij
Hier kom je te werken
Bijzonderheden
Over de functiegroep
Stel gerust je vraag

Dit ga je doen

Binnen de afdeling Planning van de NVWA bouwen we aan de toekomst: een slimme, datagedreven werkwijze voor de inzet en planning van onze medewerkers en om die waar te maken, zoeken we een data engineer Workforce Management (WFM). In deze rol zorg jij voor het datafundament waarmee we beter kunnen sturen op capaciteit, inzet en prestaties van onze inspecteurs en toezichthoudend dierenartsen. Je ontsluit en koppelt gegevens uit verschillende systemen en zorgt ervoor dat deze betrouwbaar, actueel en bruikbaar beschikbaar zijn voor analyses, dashboards en verdere datagedreven toepassingen. Daarmee speel je een sleutelrol in het versterken van onze stuurkracht op capaciteit, inzet en prestaties. En je draagt direct bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van Workforce Management, gericht op voorspelbaarder plannen, het verhogen van de kwaliteit en het realiseren van stabiele processen.

Jouw kerntaken

Als data engineer WFM beweeg je op het snijvlak van planning, data en informatievoorziening. Je begrijpt hoe gegevens worden gebruikt binnen Planning, maar jouw belangrijkste verantwoordelijkheid ligt bij het technisch ontsluiten, koppelen en beschikbaar stellen van data. Je zorgt ervoor dat gegevens uit verschillende bronsystemen op een betrouwbare en herleidbare manier beschikbaar komen voor analisten, data scientists en dashboards.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:

Datapijplijnen bouwen en beheren. Je ontwikkelt en onderhoudt datapijplijnen op Azure, zodat gegevens uit verschillende systemen betrouwbaar worden verwerkt en beschikbaar gesteld.
Data ontsluiten en koppelen. Je verdiept je in bestaande bronsystemen en de gegevens over roosters, beschikbaarheid, inzet en werkvoorraad. Je zorgt ervoor dat deze gegevens op een bruikbare en herleidbare manier worden ontsloten.
Datakwaliteit en architectuur verbeteren. Je maakt zelfstandig keuzes over onder andere datamodellering, historisering, testbaarheid en onderhoudbaarheid. Daarbij kijk je zowel naar de hoofdlijnen als naar de details van dataprocessen.
Veilige gegevensverwerking waarborgen. Je houdt rekening met privacy en informatiebeveiliging. Met onder andere dataclassificatie en rolgebaseerde toegangsrechten zorg je ervoor dat persoonsgegevens alleen toegankelijk zijn voor bevoegde medewerkers.
Dataprocessen monitoren en documenteren. Je zorgt ervoor dat datapijplijnen niet alleen werken, maar ook goed worden bewaakt, gedocumenteerd en overdraagbaar zijn.
Samenwerken met collega's en gebruikers. Je zoekt actief de verbinding met collega's van Informatievoorziening, data en ICT en met de gebruikers binnen Planning. Je legt technische keuzes helder uit, ook aan collega's zonder technische achtergrond.

Je werkt in een omgeving waarin de informatiebehoefte kan veranderen. Bij een verstoring van de dataverwerking of een onverwachte vraag naar nieuwe stuurinformatie schakel je snel en zorg je voor een werkbare en verantwoorde oplossing. Je opereert daarbij vanuit afdeling Planning, waarbij je direct samenwerkt met collega’s binnen en buiten je team. Dat doe je hybride, vanuit het hoofdkantoor van de NVWA in Utrecht of je eigen thuiskantoor.

Wil je met jouw technische kennis er voor zorgen dat data betrouwbaar beschikbaar is en dat onze collega's binnen Planning beter onderbouwde keuzes kunnen maken? En herken je jezelf in de onderstaande functie-eisen? Dan zien we graag je sollicitatie tegemoet. Zet je idealen om in daden en kom werken bij de NVWA.

Dit krijg je

Schaal 12 €4.818 - €7.094 (bruto)
Arbeidsovereenkomst voor bepaalde tijd
2 jaar
32 - 36 uur
Het salaris is gebaseerd op een werkweek van 36 uur.

Dit bieden we nog meer

Naast een inwerkprogramma dat past bij jouw functie en ruime opleidings- en/of coaching mogelijkheden voor jouw verdere professionele ontwikkeling, bieden we ook de onderstaande secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden:

Individueel Keuze Budget

Je krijgt een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB) van 16,50% van je bruto jaarsalaris. Je kunt je IKB bijvoorbeeld laten uitbetalen, bijvoorbeeld per maand of per jaar, maar je kunt ook extra verlofuren kopen. Daarnaast kun je je IKB gebruiken om belastingvrij een (elektrische) fiets voor woon-werkverkeer aan te schaffen, je thuiskantoor in te richten, fiscaal voordelig je studieschuld af te lossen tot een max van €2000,- per jaar of zelfs je woning te verduurzamen. Om dit aan te moedigen biedt de Rijksoverheid bovenop het IKB hierbij ook een werkgeversbijdrage.

Vakantiedagen

Per jaar heb je recht op 144 vakantie-uren en 64 IKB-verlofuren, wanneer je 36 uur per week werkt. Werk je meer of minder? Dan worden deze uren naar verhouding berekend. En heb je wat minder behoefte aan vakantie? Dan kun je je er ook voor kiezen om je 64 IKB-verlofuren uit te laten betalen of laten toevoegen aan je IKB-spaarverlof

Reiskostenvergoeding

Je ontvangt een mobiliteitskaart waarmee je voor woon-werk verkeer 2e klas met de trein kunt reizen. Daarnaast kun je deze gebruiken voor dienstreizen indien je naar andere locaties moet voor je werk. Ga je met de fiets naar het werk? Dan ontvang je per gefietste kilometer een reiskostenvergoeding.

Indien het voor je werkzaamheden noodzakelijk is kun je onder bepaalde voorwaarden, die staan in de sub-autoregeling van de NVWA, in aanmerking komen voor een elektrische dienstauto. Dit betreft geen persoonlijke arbeidsvoorwaarde maar een dienstauto wordt ter beschikking gesteld op basis van de sub-autoregeling van de NVWA. Deze dienstauto mag je op basis van de bijtelling plus een eigen bijdrage ook privé gebruiken.

Verlofregelingen

Voor verschillende situaties kent het Rijk verlofregelingen, zoals (aanvullend) geboorteverlof (maximaal 5 weken 100% doorbetaald), ouderschapsverlof (maximaal 9 weken 100% doorbetaald in het eerste jaar en aanvullend 75% voor 4 weken), zorgverlof en adoptie-/pleegzorgverlof.

Pensioen

De Rijksoverheid heeft een aantrekkelijke pensioensregeling bij ABP, het Algemeen Burgerlijk Pensioenfonds. Lees hier meer over de pensioensregeling bij ABP.

Extra toeslagen en vergoedingen

Voor sommige functies bij de NVWA is het nodig om buiten de reguliere kantoortijden te werken of bereikbaar te zijn. Daar staan echter ook extra toeslagen of vergoedingen tegenover. Zo kennen wij een toelage bereikbaarheids- en beschikbaarheidsdienst en een toelage onregelmatige dienst.

Dit vragen wij

Je bent een ervaren data engineer die zelfstandig technische oplossingen kan ontwikkelen en daarbij verder kijkt dan alleen de techniek. Je doorgrondt dataprocessen, ziet waar verbeteringen mogelijk zijn en maakt weloverwogen keuzes over de inrichting en kwaliteit van dataoplossingen. Je werkt zorgvuldig, hebt oog voor privacy en beveiliging en vindt het belangrijk dat jouw oplossingen betrouwbaar en goed overdraagbaar zijn. Je kunt technische vraagstukken vertalen naar begrijpelijke uitleg en werkt graag samen met zowel technische collega's als gebruikers uit de praktijk. Je bent bovendien wendbaar: als de situatie daarom vraagt, kun je snel schakelen en prioriteiten verleggen. Affiniteit met planning, capaciteitsmanagement of andere operationele bedrijfsprocessen is belangrijk, maar ervaring met een specifiek Workforce Management-systeem is geen vereiste. Je bent vooral bereid je te verdiepen in onze bestaande systemen en de gegevens die daaruit voortkomen.

Daarnaast beschik je over:

Minimaal vijf jaar relevante werkervaring als data engineer of in een vergelijkbare functie.
Aantoonbare ervaring met het bouwen van datapijplijnen op Azure, bijvoorbeeld met BI Studio en Azure Data Factory.
Ervaring met Azure Data Lake Storage als opslaglaag.
Goede kennis van Python en SQL.
Een afgeronde hbo-opleiding in informatica, data engineering, software engineering of een vergelijkbare richting is een pré. Heb je niet de genoemde opleidingsachtergrond, maar spreekt deze functie je aan en kun je jouw kennis en ervaring goed onderbouwen? Ook dan nodigen we je uit om te reageren en in je motivatie toe te lichten waarom deze functie bij je past.

Competenties

Analyseren
Plannen en organiseren
Creativiteit
Flexibiliteit

De functie heeft een looptijd van twee jaar. Om de ontwikkeling van datamanagement binnen de organisatie een extra impuls te geven, is hiervoor aanvullend budget beschikbaar gesteld. De functie is specifiek gericht op de afdeling Planning en heeft als doel de verdere ontwikkeling en professionalisering van datamanagement binnen deze afdeling te versnellen. Hoewel er geen garanties kunnen worden gegeven over een vervolg na deze periode, verwachten we dat de expertise en ervaring van de beoogde kandidaat goede mogelijkheden bieden om na afloop van de twee jaar een passende vervolgstap binnen de organisatie te vinden.

De NVWA werkt hard aan een maatschappelijk representatief personeelsbestand en hecht veel waarde aan een inclusief aannamebeleid. Wij moedigen daarom iedereen aan om te solliciteren, ongeacht (culturele)achtergrond, leeftijd, genderidentiteit, religie, Arbeidsbijzonderheid of geaardheid.

Hier kom je te werken

Meer over Handelstoezicht

Je werkt binnen de afdeling Planning van de NVWA. De afdeling telt ruim 30 medewerkers en is verantwoordelijk voor het inplannen van > 1000 toezichthouders die op verschillende locaties in het land werkzaam zijn. Binnen je functie werk je nauw samen met collega’s van Informatievoorziening, data, functioneel beheer en ICT.

De afdeling werkt landelijk, met vaste ontmoetingslocaties op de NVWA-kantoren in Eindhoven, Zwolle, Utrecht en Veenendaal. Hybride werken is mogelijk, afhankelijk van de werkzaamheden en de afstemming binnen het team.

Over Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA)

We vinden het in Nederland heel normaal dat de producten die we gebruiken en alles wat wij eten veilig is. Dat dieren goed worden behandeld, ook als ze voor de slacht bestemd zijn. Groente en fruit willen we gedachteloos kunnen consumeren en ook andere producten zijn ‘natuurlijk’ in orde. We willen onbekommerd in de natuur kunnen wandelen en speelgoed voor onze kinderen kopen zonder achterdocht. Als consumenten vertrouwen we daar gewoon op, voor ons is dat vanzelfsprekend.

Maar we vergeten soms dat bedrijven dagelijks hard werken aan die hoge standaard. Dat het voor ondernemers niet altijd makkelijk is om aan alle geldende wet- en regelgeving te voldoen. We vergeten ook dat de overheid daarop toeziet. Veiligheid klinkt zo eenvoudig, maar dat is het niet.

Wat doet de NVWA?

De medewerkers van de Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA) werken dagelijks hard om die standaard te behouden. In gesprek met ondernemers in de horeca, de slachterijen, de plantenteelt en met andere producenten ziet de NVWA toe op de voedsel- en productveiligheid, plantgezondheid en het welzijn van dieren, natuur en milieu. Met (inter)nationale wet- en regelgeving in de hand. We gaan uit van vertrouwen, maar tegen ondernemers die het niet zo nauw nemen, treden we stevig op. In het belang van de samenleving.

Wij kijken scherp waar de grootste risico’s zitten en waar toezicht het hardst nodig is, zodat we consumenten en anderen tijdig kunnen informeren. Ook heeft de NVWA een belangrijke rol bij exportkeuringen en bij de import van producten in Europa.

Waar staat de NVWA voor?

De NVWA is verantwoordelijk voor het toezicht op dierenwelzijn, diergezondheid, voedselveiligheid, productveiligheid, tabaks- en alcoholontmoediging, plantgezondheid en natuur en milieu.

De Rijksoverheid streeft ernaar een werkgever te zijn waar iedere medewerker, ongeacht leeftijd, sekse, geaardheid, etnische afkomst en arbeidsbeperking voor wil werken. Werken aan maatschappelijke vraagstukken in divers samengestelde teams maakt ons effectiever en innovatiever. Dat maakt het werk waardevol en uitdagend.

Bij de NVWA vragen we van medewerkers flexibiliteit om mee te bewegen met veranderende pr

jobs.title: Risk Analyst B2B (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Company Description

Everyone’s story matters. Come shape your story with us at Riverty.

But where does that take you?

To one of our 30 hybrid workspaces – designed for exchanging ideas, learning from others, and shaping the way we work. An international community of over 4,000 people, representing almost 80 nationalities across 11 countries. United by one mission: Combining empathy, advanced technology and data-driven insights to keep people and businesses in flow. With payments made for them. So that they don’t have to worry about it.

And there’s more.
We are part of the family-owned Bertelsmann group. Established. Corporate. In a fast-paced industry. We enable flexible payments in various industries, simplifying the financial management of known brands and helping people repay debt to build financial confidence. In short: shaping FinTech.

Job Description

We are looking for a

Risk Analyst – B2B (m/f/d) (unlimited, full-time)

Join our team at our location in Berlin, Verl, Amsterdam, Heerenveen, Luxembourg – flexible working conditions available

We are looking for a Risk Analyst – B2B for our Risk Analytics team in the Client Underwriting Unit with a hands-on attitude that is keen to have an impact on our risk assessment by mitigating risk in terms of affordability / solvency for the B2B end customer in a balanced risk decision environment.

The focus of the team lies on contributing to the definition of our risk strategy in the B2B space, its (further) development and the constant monitoring and steering according to it.

In line with Riverty's overarching vision to become the most human-centric FinTech, the Risk Analytics team develops appropriate customer risk strategies for different markets and ecosystems. The organization is characterized by technology-based rapid learning and decision-making cycles and guided by a strong common purpose to jointly create value for all stakeholders. Strong footprint in DACH/NL & Nordics with further expansion ambition within Europe, e. g. UK , Italy.

The Main Responsibilities Are

Lead the redesign of B2B underwriting models, including scorecards, decision engines, rule sets, and rating methodologies.
Continuous improvement of underlying data analysis and existing business processes to support our B2B product expansion in new countries.
Build harmonized multi-country credit frameworks while adapting strategies to local market dynamics, regulations, and data availability.
Establish best practices for ad-hoc & deep-dive analyses.
Partner with Data Science to build and deploy next-generation ML-based credit models for customers in the B2B space.
Enhance reporting frameworks, dashboards, and risk KPIs to support leadership decision-making.
You will work in close collaboration with other functions such as Risk Product, Fraud Risk Steering, Data Science, Finance, etc.
The function is reporting into the Risk Analytics & Steering Lead, which is reporting into the Functional Unit Lead for Client Underwriting.
The location is flexible, preferred locations are Germany (Berlin, Verl), Luxembourg or the Netherlands (Amsterdam, Heerenveen).

Qualifications

What you should bring:

Significant experience in B2B risk analytics, ideally within BNPL, lending, payments, or fintech.
Relevant experience in a credit risk management environment.
Expertise in using various programming languages (SQL / Python / R) to perform complex analytical tasks.
Experience in working in an international, agile, cross-functional environment.
You embrace new technology and understand the potential of data and advanced analytics.
You are a strategic thinker with vision and a strong operator - you get things done.
Language: English (mandatory); German or Dutch is a plus.
